meanings: a leaf (of a tree, of a bough); pl. flenneth, leaves; the tree's leaf beside the guild's sheet and page (a new sense of O0614)
derivation: a new sense of canon flenn (O0614), from the root's own sense, *xwle- 'a thin sheet: a leaf' (*xwlen-naʔ > Hal hwlennā > flenn): the Shore kept the word for the slate's leaf and the book's, and a leaf of a tree is the same thin thing; its regular plural is flenneth (slender), apart from the lexicalised broad flennath, the Book. Made for Halyna's reading of IV.4 (Book v3), 'Leaves. No — words, like leaves.', Flenneth. Nel — brodath, hosen flenneth: the English leaf works twice, and so does the Orrowen [wf12 unit W03]
